newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BRIGHTON SACK CASE, FANS VOW TO CONTINUE PROTESTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRIGHTON SACK CASE, FANS VOW TO CONTINUE PROTESTS.

text.p: English crisis club Brighton and Hove Albion sacked manager Jimmy Case on Wednesday but angry fans said the move would not resolve the third division side's mounting problems.

Case, who played in the great Liverpool side of the late 1970s and early 1980s, was dismissed in the wake of Brighton's 3-2 home defeat to Darlington on Tuesday, a result which keeps the south coast side 92nd in the 92-team English football league.
Brighton, F.A. Cup finalists in 1983, were knocked out of this season's cup by non-League Sudbury last month and Case acknowledged on Wednesday that the club's headaches "were just not going away".

The club has to move from its Goldstone Ground at the end of this season and does not have a permanent home to go to. Its fans have staged a series of protests and pitch invasions in a bid to force chairman Bill Archer and chief executive David Bellotti to resign.
Bellotti said Case, who had been in charge at Brighton for one year, was sacked because of the side's poor results.

"It is of paramount importance we appoint a manager to take us off the bottom of division three," he said. "We also appeal to all supporters to put differences with the directors to one side and support the new manager and players."
But supporters showed no sign of heeding Bellotti's appeal.

"We are a long way off a solution and the whole future of the club is hanging in the balance," Paul Samrah of the Brighton Independent Supporters' Association said. "It requires a change of direction and ownership of the club as we have repeatedly stated."
